programmes.name_local: A*ccelerate (A*STAR technology commercialisation and spin-off support)
programmes.name_en: A*ccelerate Technology Commercialisation and Spin-off Support
programmes.amount_note: Licensing of A*STAR intellectual property to spin-offs and startups, with A*ccelerate typically taking equity and/or royalties, plus gap funding for translational work. Quantum is deal-specific.
programmes.deadline_note: Rolling; driven by IP availability and spin-off formation timelines.

procedure_steps.detail: Identify the A*STAR technology of interest via the A*ccelerate technology portfolio.
Discuss licensing terms and translational plan with the A*ccelerate team.
Negotiate the licence and, for spin-offs, the founding equity structure.
Apply for gap or translational funding where applicable.

eligibility.other_note: Startups licensing or spinning out A*STAR-owned intellectual property.

programmes.source_snippet: A*ccelerate translates A*STAR research into products and companies through licensing and spin-offs.

programmes.name_local: A*STAR GET-Up (Growing Enterprises through Technology Upgrade)
programmes.funder: Agency for Science, Technology and Research (A*STAR)
programmes.amount_note: Includes T-Up secondment of A*STAR research scientists and engineers into companies with salary support of up to 70% of the seconded officer's cost, plus Operation and Technology Roadmapping and technology consultancy.
programmes.deadline_note: Rolling; secondment scope negotiated with the relevant A*STAR research institute.

procedure_steps.detail: Contact A*STAR to discuss the technology gap and the profile of officer required.
Agree the secondment scope, duration and deliverables with the host research institute.
Submit the T-Up application for salary support.
Officer is seconded into the company, typically for up to two years.

eligibility.other_note: Singapore-registered SMEs with at least 30% local shareholding and group turnover/headcount within SME limits.

programmes.source_snippet: GET-Up helps local enterprises upgrade their technology capabilities through secondment of A*STAR research scientists and engineers.

programmes.funder: Agency for Science, Technology and Research (A*STAR)
programmes.amount_note: Subsidised access to A*STAR's advanced manufacturing equipment plus user training and advisory hours. Not a cash grant; subsidy is applied to the equipment usage fee.
programmes.deadline_note: Rolling enquiries and bookings through the A*STAR Advanced Remanufacturing and Technology Centre / Tech Access team.

procedure_steps.detail: Identify the required equipment from the Tech Access catalogue.
Submit an enquiry describing the intended process or prototype.
Scoping discussion with A*STAR engineers and quotation.
Training, then supervised or self-service equipment use.

eligibility.other_note: Singapore-registered SMEs; at least 30% local shareholding for the subsidised rate.

programmes.source_snippet: Tech Access provides SMEs with access to advanced manufacturing equipment, user training and expert advice.

programmes.name_local: Enterprise Development and Growth Enabler (EDGE) Grant
programmes.name_en: Enterprise Development and Growth Enabler (EDGE) Grant
programmes.amount_note: Announced at Budget 2026 as a single consolidated grant replacing EDG, MRA and PSG. Support of up to S$100,000 per company per year for eligible activities; international expansion support rises to 70% for SMEs and 50% for non-SMEs. Larger or bespoke projects continue to be handled case-by-case by Enterprise Singapore outside the EDGE cap.
programmes.deadline_note: Not yet open. Enterprise Singapore states 'EDGE launches in 2H2026. Existing grants (EDG, MRA, PSG) remain accessible until launch.' Exact launch date and full guidelines had not been published as at 14 August 2026.
programmes.reopen_note: Launches in the second half of 2026, replacing EDG, MRA and PSG. Applicants with imminent projects are advised to apply under the existing schemes rather than wait, since EDG/MRA/PSG remain open until the switch-over. The MRA 'new market' restriction is removed under EDGE and the Double Tax Deduction for Internationalisation expenditure cap rises from S$150,000 to S$400,000.

procedure_steps.detail: Monitor the Enterprise Singapore Budget 2026 and financial support pages for the EDGE launch and detailed guidelines.
Until launch, apply under EDG, MRA or PSG for projects that cannot wait.
From launch, apply via the Business Grants Portal under a single EDGE application.

documents_required.note: Expect Business Grants Portal application, ACRA profile, financials and project proposal in line with EDG/MRA practice

eligibility.other_note: Full eligibility rules not yet published as at August 2026. Expected to follow existing Enterprise Singapore criteria: Singapore-registered and operating, with local shareholding thresholds determining the higher support tier.

programmes.source_snippet: EDGE launches in 2H2026. Existing grants (EDG, MRA, PSG) remain accessible until launch.

programmes.amount_note: Loans of up to S$8 million per borrower for high-growth enterprises, with Enterprise Singapore sharing a portion of the default risk with participating financial institutions (risk share typically 50%, higher for young companies). Interest rate is set by the lender.
programmes.deadline_note: Rolling; applications are made to a participating financial institution rather than to Enterprise Singapore.

procedure_steps.detail: Approach a participating financial institution offering EFS-Venture Debt.
Submit the business plan, financials and funding history.
Lender credit assessment; Enterprise Singapore risk share applied.
Facility agreement and drawdown, typically with warrants attached.

eligibility.other_note: Singapore-registered and physically present in Singapore, at least 30% local shareholding, group revenue not exceeding S$500m.

programmes.source_snippet: The Enterprise Financing Scheme covers seven areas including Venture Debt to support high-growth enterprises.

programmes.amount_note: Support level, not a fixed cap: from 1 April 2023 SMEs can receive up to 50% support for EDG; sustainability-related projects are supported at up to 70%. EDG funds qualifying project costs, namely third-party consultancy fees, software and equipment, and internal manpower cost. There is no published per-project ceiling; the award follows the approved project cost. Projects are supported on a reimbursement basis.
programmes.deadline_note: Open continuously on the Business Grants Portal; each complete application takes approximately 8-12 weeks to process. Note: EnterpriseSG states that EDGE launches in 2H2026 and that existing grants (EDG, MRA, PSG) remain accessible until that launch, so this scheme is expected to be superseded.

procedure_steps.detail: Identify the project category: Core Capabilities, Innovation & Productivity, or Market Access.
If claiming management consultancy costs, engage a consultant with SAC-accredited TR 43 or SS 680 certification.
Prepare the project proposal using the EnterpriseSG template and gather supporting documents.
Apply on the Business Grants Portal using a Corppass account before the project commences.
On completion, appoint an auditor from EnterpriseSG's Pre-Qualified Panel and file the claim within six months of the end of the project qualifying period.

documents_required.doc: Latest ACRA search or instant information
documents_required.note: Dated no earlier than 6 months from date of project application

documents_required.doc: Audited financial statements or certified management accounts for the last financial year
Consolidated financial statements of the ultimate parent company

documents_required.note: Use the EnterpriseSG template for the chosen category

documents_required.doc: Proof of quotation for project cost items
Consultants' CVs and SAC-accredited TR 43 or SS 680 certificates

eligibility.other_note: Business entity registered and operating in Singapore; at least 30% local equity held directly or indirectly by Singaporeans and/or Singapore PRs, determined by ultimate individual ownership; company financially ready to start and complete the project. Projects must be new, must not have commenced, and must not be generating revenue at the point of grant application. Third party companies are not allowed to apply or manage the grant on behalf of applicant companies. There are no compulsory application fees.

programmes.source_snippet: From 1 April 2023, SMEs can receive up to 50% support for EDG (support period for sustainability-related projects has been extended, and will be supported at up to 70%). ... EDGE launches in 2H2026. Existing grants (EDG, MRA, PSG) remain accessible until launch.

programmes.amount_note: Enhanced tax deductions/allowances of up to 400% on the first S$400,000 of qualifying expenditure per Year of Assessment across five activity categories (qualifying R&D in Singapore, IP registration, IP acquisition/licensing, approved training, and innovation projects with polytechnics/ITE). Eligible businesses may instead opt for a non-taxable cash payout of up to S$20,000 in lieu of deductions.
programmes.deadline_note: Claimed through the annual Corporate Income Tax return (Form C-S/C). The scheme was legislated for Years of Assessment 2024 to 2028; the cash payout option must be elected by the relevant filing deadline.

procedure_steps.detail: Identify and document qualifying innovation expenditure during the financial year.
Decide whether to claim enhanced deductions or elect the cash payout conversion.
File the claim in the annual Corporate Income Tax return via myTax Portal.
Retain supporting documentation for IRAS review.

documents_required.doc: R&D claim form and technical project write-up where R&D is claimed
Invoices and payment records for qualifying expenditure

eligibility.other_note: Singapore tax-resident businesses carrying on a trade or business. The cash payout option requires at least three local employees earning CPF contributions in the relevant period.

programmes.source_snippet: The Enterprise Innovation Scheme provides enhanced tax deductions or allowances for businesses that undertake qualifying innovation activities.

programmes.amount_note: Up to 70% of eligible costs for local SMEs (the 70% level takes effect 1 April 2026), capped at S$100,000 per company per new market, split across three activities: overseas market promotion up to S$20,000; overseas business development up to S$50,000; overseas market set-up up to S$30,000.
programmes.deadline_note: Open continuously on the Business Grants Portal. EnterpriseSG states that EDGE launches in 2H2026 and that existing grants (EDG, MRA, PSG) remain accessible until launch.

procedure_steps.detail: Identify the target overseas market where annual sales have not exceeded S$100,000 in any of the past three years.
Select the activity (market promotion, business development, or market set-up) and a vendor, and obtain quotations.
Apply on the Business Grants Portal with a Corppass account before the activity starts.
Complete the project, then submit the claim with the required audit.

documents_required.doc: Latest audited financial statements or management accounts
Vendor quotation for the proposed activity
Project proposal describing the target market and activity

eligibility.other_note: Registered and operating in Singapore; at least 30% local equity held directly or indirectly by Singaporeans and/or Singapore PRs; new to the target market, with annual sales not exceeding S$100,000 in that market in any of the prior three years; Group Annual Sales Turnover not exceeding S$100 million OR Group employment size not exceeding 200 employees.

programmes.source_snippet: Up to 70% of eligible costs for local SMEs ... capped at S$100,000 per company per new market ... At least 30% local equity held directly or indirectly by Singaporean(s) and/or Singapore PR(s) ... Group Annual Sales Turnover not exceeding S$100 million OR a Group employment size not exceeding 200 employees.

programmes.amount_note: Translational gap funding of up to S$5 million per project (typically over up to three years) to bridge publicly funded research towards a commercial product or spin-off. Applications are submitted through the host Institution of Higher Learning or Research Institute.
programmes.deadline_note: Proposals are received through host institutions' innovation and enterprise offices, which run internal cut-offs before submission to NRF. NRF does not publish a single public deadline.

procedure_steps.detail: Work with the technology transfer / innovation and enterprise office of the host university or research institute.
Prepare the commercialisation proposal with milestones and a route to spin-off or licensing.
Host institution submits to NRF.
NRF panel evaluation and award; milestone-based disbursement.

eligibility.other_note: Applications must be led by researchers at Singapore Institutions of Higher Learning, Research Institutes or A*STAR entities; spin-off companies benefit as the eventual vehicle rather than applying directly.

programmes.source_snippet: The Central Gap Fund supports the translation of publicly funded research towards commercialisation.

programmes.funder: Enterprise Singapore with sector lead agencies, administered via GoBusiness / Business Grants Portal
programmes.amount_note: PSG defrays the cost of pre-scoped IT solutions, equipment and consultancy services from pre-approved vendors. The GoBusiness PSG page describes the two support types (sector-specific and generic solutions) and the eligibility rules but does not state the support percentage or a cap on that page, so those are recorded as null rather than guessed; per-solution support levels are shown in the PSG Solution Directory.
programmes.deadline_note: Open continuously. EnterpriseSG states that EDGE launches in 2H2026 and that existing grants (EDG, MRA, PSG) remain accessible until launch.

procedure_steps.detail: Search the PSG Solution Directory for supportable solutions for your sector.
Get a quotation from the pre-approved vendor (IT solution), the vendor (equipment), or the pre-approved consultant (consultancy).
Submit the application on the Business Grants Portal using a Corppass account.
Submit the grant claim on the BGP before the claim due date.

documents_required.doc: Invoice and payment proof at claim stage

eligibility.other_note: Registered and operating in Singapore; the purchase/lease/subscription of the IT solution, equipment or consultancy service must be used in Singapore. For selected solutions only: minimum 30% local shareholding. For consultancy service solutions only: at least three local employees at the point of application. Companies are reminded not to share their Corppass with vendors to submit applications or claims.

programmes.source_snippet: Registered and operating in Singapore. Purchase/lease/subscription of the IT solutions/equipment/consultancy service must be used in Singapore. For selected solutions only: Have a minimum of 30% local shareholding. For consultancy service solutions only: Have at least three local employees at the point of application.

programmes.amount_note: A two-year customised growth programme for high-potential local companies, delivered with appointed programme partners. Support is largely advisory and capability-building; associated project costs may be supported under EDG.
programmes.deadline_note: Cohort-based intake; Enterprise Singapore and its programme partners announce intakes periodically.

procedure_steps.detail: Submit an expression of interest to Enterprise Singapore or a programme partner.
Diagnostic assessment of growth readiness.
Selection into the cohort and co-development of a growth roadmap.
Two-year execution with partner support.

eligibility.other_note: Singapore-registered companies with at least 30% local shareholding, demonstrated growth track record and ambition to scale regionally or globally.

programmes.source_snippet: Scale-Up SG helps high-growth local companies build capabilities to become future global champions.

programmes.name_en: SGInnovate Deep Tech Talent and Venture Building Programmes
programmes.amount_note: SGInnovate provides deep tech talent programmes (Summation, Helix Immersion, apprenticeships and PhD/fellowship talent pipelines) and selective early-stage co-investment into Singapore deep tech companies. Investment amounts are deal-specific and not published as a fixed grant quantum.
programmes.deadline_note: Talent programmes run in cohorts with their own intake windows; investment enquiries are rolling.

procedure_steps.detail: Review SGInnovate's current programmes and open cohorts.
Apply to the relevant talent programme or submit an investment enquiry.
Screening and interview / due diligence.
Programme placement or investment closing.

documents_required.doc: CV and academic record for talent programmes

eligibility.other_note: Focus on Singapore-based deep tech ventures and talent; SGInnovate is wholly owned by the Singapore Government.

programmes.source_snippet: SGInnovate builds and scales deep tech ventures in Singapore through talent, capital and community programmes.

programmes.amount_note: Funding support to incubators and accelerators (not directly to startups) for programme operating costs and mentor/expert costs. Startups benefit indirectly by joining a supported accelerator. Support quantum is negotiated per operator.
programmes.deadline_note: Rolling assessment of incubator/accelerator applications; startups apply to the accelerator's own cohort intake, not to Enterprise Singapore.

procedure_steps.detail: Incubator/accelerator submits a programme proposal to Enterprise Singapore via the Business Grants Portal.
Assessment of track record, mentor network and value-add to portfolio startups.
Award and funding agreement; operator runs cohorts.
Startups apply directly to the supported accelerator's cohort.

eligibility.other_note: Applicant is the incubator/accelerator operator, which must be Singapore-based with a credible track record. Startups access it by joining a supported programme.

programmes.source_snippet: Startup SG Accelerator supports incubators and accelerators in enhancing their programmes for startups.

programmes.funder: Enterprise Singapore, deployed through SG Growth Capital (SGGC) and SGInnovate (SGI)
programmes.amount_note: Government co-invests alongside independent, qualified third-party investors. SSGE investment cap for each deep tech startup is S$12 million. Co-investment ratio (SGGC/SGI : co-investor), as of 27 Feb 2026: 2:1 up to the first S$1 million; 1:1 thereafter up to S$4 million; 1:2 thereafter up to S$8 million; 1:3 thereafter up to S$12 million. A growth-stage direct investment route and a fund-of-funds route (minimum investee fund size S$30 million) also exist.
programmes.deadline_note: Rolling. Startups do not apply to EnterpriseSG directly; they raise from an appointed co-investment partner (SGGC or SGInnovate).

procedure_steps.detail: Confirm the startup is Singapore-registered, incorporated 10 years or less, and in one of the SSGE deep tech domains.
Secure a lead from an independent qualified third-party investor.
Approach SG Growth Capital or SGInnovate to co-invest in the round at the applicable ratio.

documents_required.doc: Term sheet from the lead third-party investor
Technical and commercial due diligence pack

eligibility.other_note: A Singapore-based startup means a Singapore-registered private limited company incorporated for 10 years or less that develops or possesses innovations in Singapore. Focus domains: Advanced Manufacturing; Pharmbio/MedTech; Agrifood Tech; Sustainability (energy, circular economy, urban mobility); Spacetech; and Smart Nation and Digital Economy deep tech areas (quantum tech, cybersecurity, generative AI). Growth-stage direct investment requires prior substantial institutional capital and at least one other institutional investor in the round.

programmes.source_snippet: SSGE Investment Cap for each deep tech startup S$12 million. Co-investment Ratio (SGGC /SGI: co-investor) 2:1 up to the first S$1 million; 1:1 thereafter, up to S$4 million; 1:2 thereafter, up to S$8 million; 1:3 thereafter, up to S$12 million. As of 27 Feb 2026.

programmes.amount_note: With effect from 1 April 2024 EnterpriseSG supports all successful startup grant recipients on a 1:1 support ratio, for a grant amount from S$20,000 to S$50,000. Applicants must inject co-matching paid-up capital into the startup at a 1:1 ratio to the grant quantum. Co-matching capital may originate from an AMP's or third party's investment (e.g. convertible / SAFE notes) in lieu of paid-up capital, but at least 50% of the co-matching capital must be paid-up capital on ACRA Bizfile when the application is submitted to EnterpriseSG.
programmes.deadline_note: Rolling: startups apply first to an Accredited Mentor Partner (AMP), then submit to EnterpriseSG once they hold a Letter of Recommendation. A separate Call for Partnerships 2026 is open for organisations wanting to become AMPs.

procedure_steps.detail: Complete recognised entrepreneurship training and prepare the business idea.
Apply to an Accredited Mentor Partner within 6 months of incorporating the private limited entity (or before incorporating).
Obtain a Letter of Recommendation from the AMP and submit the application to EnterpriseSG.
Inject the 1:1 co-matching capital and receive the grant; second tranche disbursed on a separate form.

documents_required.doc: Letter of Recommendation from an Accredited Mentor Partner
documents_required.note: Application cannot be submitted without it

documents_required.doc: ACRA Bizfile showing shareholding and paid-up capital
documents_required.note: At least 50% of co-matching capital must appear as paid-up capital

eligibility.other_note: Open to Singapore Citizens / Permanent Residents. The first applicant must be a first-time founder with no prior Private Limited entity with ACRA, must not be externally employed, must commit full time, and must have undergone entrepreneurship training; a second applicant need not be a first-time founder and may be externally employed. First-time founders must hold a minimum of 30% equity collectively and both applicants must hold equity. The startup must have at least 51% of issued shares owned by SC/PR, be registered as a private limited entity in Singapore for less than 6 months at the point of application to the AMP, keep key HQ activities mainly in Singapore, and must not have received funding from another government organisation for the same idea. Excluded ideas: cafes, restaurants, night clubs, lounges, bars, foot reflexology, massage parlours, gambling, prostitution, social escort services, employment agencies and geomancy.

programmes.source_snippet: Applicants are required to inject co-matching paid-up capital into the startup at a 1:1 ratio to match the grant quantum that they are applying for. ... Be registered as a private limited entity in Singapore for less than 6 months at point of application to AMP ... Has minimum 51% of issued shares are owned by Singapore Citizen (SC) /Singapore Permanent Resident (PR)

programmes.amount_note: Umbrella of talent schemes rather than a cash grant: EntrePass (work pass for foreign founders), Tech@SG (facilitated Employment Pass sponsorship for fast-growing tech firms), T-Up (secondment of A*STAR research scientists and engineers with salary subsidy of up to 70%), and the Startup SG Talent Global Founder Programme.
programmes.deadline_note: Each component has its own rolling application route (MOM for EntrePass, EnterpriseSG/EDB for Tech@SG, A*STAR for T-Up).

procedure_steps.detail: Identify the relevant component: EntrePass, Tech@SG or T-Up.
For EntrePass, apply through the Ministry of Manpower with the venture's funding/IP/incubation evidence.
For Tech@SG, apply through the Tech@SG portal evidencing funding raised from recognised investors.
For T-Up, agree a secondment scope with A*STAR and apply for the salary subsidy.

documents_required.doc: Evidence of funding raised or IP ownership

eligibility.other_note: Requirements differ by component; Tech@SG requires a minimum funding raised from recognised investors, EntrePass requires the applicant to be a foreign entrepreneur meeting innovation/funding criteria.

programmes.source_snippet: Startup SG Talent helps startups attract and retain talent through schemes such as EntrePass, Tech@SG and T-Up.

programmes.name_en: Startup SG Tech (Proof-of-Concept and Proof-of-Value grants)
programmes.amount_note: Proof-of-Concept (POC) grant cap SGD 400,000 (raised from SGD 250,000 for formal Stage 2 applications submitted from 2 Jan 2025); Proof-of-Value (POV) grant cap SGD 800,000 (raised from SGD 500,000 on the same date). Startups must demonstrate existing paid-up capital equivalent to at least 10% of the POC grant, or at least 20% of the POV grant. Grants are awarded upon completion of each milestone. The grant carries a share subscription component: EnterpriseSG or its appointed nominee has the right to subscribe to shares equivalent to 50% of the awarded grant amount, up to 49% of total shareholding, exercised when a qualifying equity financing round occurs.
programmes.deadline_note: Competitive grant with a rolling two-stage intake: Registration of Interest (Stage 1), then formal Stage 2 application.

procedure_steps.detail: Download and complete the Startup SG Tech Registration of Interest form.
Submit the form via the EnterpriseSG enquiry channel.
If invited, submit the formal Stage 2 application with full project and cost details.
On award, deliver against milestones; grant is disbursed per milestone.

documents_required.doc: Technical project proposal demonstrating proprietary technology and breakthrough innovation
Evidence of paid-up capital (10% of POC grant / 20% of POV grant)
Proof of interest from a potential customer or third-party investor

eligibility.other_note: Registered in Singapore within the past 10 years at time of grant application; at least 30% local equity held directly or indirectly by Singaporeans and/or Singapore PRs; company must not be a subsidiary (>50% held by a corporate parent) at point of incorporation; group annual sales turnover not more than S$100 million or group employment size not more than 200 workers; core R&D activities carried out in Singapore; main applicant must have a significant role, not be a mere shareholder. The project must not have commenced at application. Nine eligible technology areas are listed, including Advanced Manufacturing/Robotics, Biomedical Sciences and Healthcare, Clean Technology, ICT (5G, AI, cybersecurity), New Industries (AR/VR, blockchain, space, quantum), Precision Engineering, Transport Engineering, Food Science and Agritech.

programmes.source_snippet: To maintain financial discipline, startups will be required to demonstrate existing paid-up capital equivalent to at least 10% of the POC grant. The grant cap for POC will remain at SGD400,000. ... The grant cap for POV will remain at SGD800,000. ... Startup SG Tech will also include a share subscription component, where EnterpriseSG or its appointed nominee will have the right to subscribe to shares equivalent to 50% of the awarded grant amount, up to 49% of the total shareholding of the company.

programmes.amount_note: Up to S$1 million in funding is made available to winning solutions addressing urban sustainability and decarbonisation challenges, awarded as grant and/or investment depending on the solution and company stage.
programmes.deadline_note: Annual global open call. Submissions typically open in January and close around March, with the Grand Finale held in the middle of the year during Ecosperity Week.
programmes.reopen_note: Runs annually. The next call is expected to open in the first quarter of 2027; watch theliveabilitychallenge.org and Temasek Foundation announcements.

procedure_steps.detail: Register on the challenge platform when the annual call opens.
Submit the solution against the published problem statements (typically decarbonisation, food and water resilience).
Shortlisting and mentoring rounds.
Pitch at the Grand Finale; winners receive funding and deployment support.

documents_required.doc: Technical description and evidence of validation

eligibility.other_note: Open globally; solutions must be deployable in Singapore and tropical Asia. Individuals, research teams and companies may enter.

programmes.source_snippet: The Liveability Challenge is a global search for solutions to urban sustainability, with up to S$1 million in funding.
